A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same InterNeg research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison; the additional page in v3 contains an appendix contents list.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix B report original InterNeg benchmark results, component ablations, sensitivity tests and robustness analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical evaluations, including ImageNet and CIFAR benchmark results and the appendix analyses.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithms 1–2 retain the same negative-text selection, modality inversion, dynamic filtering and OOD scoring procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same ImageNet, CIFAR, ImageNet-V2 and robustness scenarios. The corrected CIFAR row label matches the dataset pairing already described in v1 Appendix B.3; it does not establish changed dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding benchmark and analysis tables, including the relocated CIFAR comparisons. Replacing 'Ours' with 'InterNeg' in Tables 11–13 identifies the same proposed method.

E3.justification: Evaluation metrics, sampling procedures, CLIP backbones and hyperparameters remain unchanged, including the CIFAR-specific M = 70,000. The dataset-label correction aligns the table with the existing protocol description.

E4.justification: Component ablations, imbalance tests, parameter sensitivity, ordering robustness, backbone comparisons, cross-domain analysis, ID error analysis and corpus sensitivity are retained. The ordering analysis moves from Appendix B.2 to B.3 without changing its evidence.

E5.justification: v1 Table 5 becomes v3 Table 9, retaining seeds 0–4, individual outcomes, means and standard deviations of 0.05 and 0.46. No uncertainty-reporting procedure or run count changes.

E6.justification: A result attribution is corrected: the near-OOD row under CIFAR100 ID changes from 'CIFAR100' in v1 Table 7 to 'CIFAR10' in v3 Table 6. Its FPR95 of 60.10 and AUROC of 84.19 remain unchanged. All other matched scores and plotted findings are retained.

T1.justification: The formal setup, Equations 1–12, distance criteria, scoring formulation and inversion loss are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, proofs or derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same distance-consistency novelty claim, two-part InterNeg contribution and performance claims, including the stated 3.47% FPR95 reduction and 5.50% Near-OOD AUROC improvement.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and interpretations remain unchanged. The zero-shot and ID-data-dependency discussion in v1 Appendix E is retained as v3 Appendix D.2, with the same applicability arguments and qualifications.

D1.justification: Algorithm 2 and Appendix C retain the same pseudocode, implementation settings, prompt template and RTX 3090 hardware disclosure. Both versions promise code at the same repository; no resource-availability change is reported.

R1.justification: Reference 72 changes from 'How to fine-tune the model: unified model shift and model bias policy optimization' (2023) to 'Scrutinize what we ignore: Reining in task representation shift of context-based offline meta reinforcement learning' (2025). Its introductory citation role and the substantive research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 adds an appendix contents list, swaps subsections B.2 and B.3, and groups the former Appendices D and E under 'Further Discussion' as D.1 and D.2. Affiliations and acknowledgements are updated; the scientific narrative is otherwise retained.

P2.justification: Appendix Tables 5–9 are reordered and renumbered, and appendix tables and Figure 5 are repaginated. Table labels receive the CIFAR correction and 'Ours' replacements. The contents page is new, while figure content and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 resolves the internally inconsistent CIFAR near-OOD label in v1 Table 7 and improves appendix navigation through a contents list and grouped discussions. These provide limited gains in reporting accuracy and accessibility; the method, numerical evidence and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
